summary: A granite keeper's house with an iron tower at the west tip of Plum Island, marking Plum Gut; lit 1827, rebuilt 1869-70, dark since 1978 and closed to the public.

access.note: Island and lighthouse closed to the public; visible from the water.

corrections.why: The USLHS lists Plum Gut only as an alternate name; the station is Plum Island Light, and the Orient Point Light (the 'Coffee Pot') is a separate structure in the Gut.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1869-70 lighthouse has been dark since 1978; a modern automated light replaced it on a separate structure, so sources differ on 'still lit' depending on which structure they mean.
USLHS gives 74.75 ft above mean high water for the old light; the record's 6.4 m likely refers to the modern shed light or a structure height.

notes_for_editor: NRHP nomination (2011, ref 11000014) is not digitised at NPGallery and the NARA catalog is off limits, so no nomination was read; the 2011 listing date comes from the record only and is not stated in the story. Corpus lacks pre-1880 Lighthouse Board reports, so the 1868 report and 1850 inspector quotes are cited to Lighthouse Friends as quoted (not read directly). Lens order conflict: sources read say fourth-order from 1856; Wikipedia (not cited) says sixth-order 1856 and fourth-order 1897. First light dispute: Lighthouse Friends says 35-ft stone tower; Ted Webb says a pole with lamps. The Commissioner 1917 table was matched by column position (Chapel and tug S. L. Hommedieu); the action text beside him could not be tied reliably, so the rescue details rest on Lighthouse Friends. Blanche's father is not named by the source; LF's 'granddaughter of Keeper Wetmore' is ambiguous between Sr. and Jr. (Sr. died 1892). Roster gaps 1949-1962 are the archive's. Newspaper searches (Chronicling America) returned nothing/timed out under shared rate limit. Light-House Board volumes 1891-1892 and 1896-1897 are two-year bound volumes; the fiscal year of the individual entries was not confirmed, so the story does not date them beyond the 1890s. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the Commissioner 1917 table row (Chapel / Tug S. L. Hommedieu / rescued captain and wife in open boat without oars) was confirmed on the page image, printed p. 55; fiscal 1917 covers July 1916-June 1917, so the calendar year may be 1916 (Lighthouse Friends says 1917).
